newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines arrests 23 HK Chinese in Spratlys.
newsitem.headline: Philippines arrests 23 HK Chinese in Spratlys.

text.p: The Philippine Navy has arrested 23 Hong Kong Chinese fishermen near the disputed Spratly Islands in the South China Sea, navy officials said on Tuesday.

The fishermen were on board the MV Cheng Lunyao owned by the East Sea International Investment Co of Hong Kong, when a Philippine Navy patrol boat apprehended them on July 31, a senior official told reporters.

The fishermen were in the vicinity of Hasahasa Shoal, about 145 km (90 miles) west of the southwestern Philippine island of Palawan when they were apprehended, the official said, asking not to be identified.
There was no official explanation for the delay in reporting the detention of the fishermen, who are being held in Puerto Princesa, capital of Palawan Island province.
The Spratlys are a cluster of potentially oil-rich isles, reefs and shoals some or all of which are claimed by China, the Philippines, Taiwan, Vietnam, Malaysia and Brunei.
Beijing says all the islands and rocky outcrops in the sea have historically belonged to China since ancient times.
"They were clearly in Philippine waters when we apprehended them," a Navy official said.
Explosive materials were found on board, he said.

A recent series of incidents involving alleged trespassing by Chinese naval and fishing vessels in areas claimed by Manila in the South China Sea has threatened to sour relations between China and the Philippines.

The Philippine Navy in May arrested 21 Chinese fishermen near Scarborough Shoal well north of the Spratlys for alleged illegal entry, but a local judge dismissed the charges and ordered their release after 52 days detention.
The judge said ownership of the shoal had not been established so there were no grounds to charge them with illegally entering Philippine waters.
